items.title: [FDD Diary #16] as any
content:
AI wrote 'as any' and jumped every wall I built.
One line. All my structure, gone.

Switched to Rust. The compiler said no.

TypeScript has types.
But 'as any' bypasses everything.
Discipline has cheaters.

Rust is a constitution. Can't be cheated.
Compiler catches it before it runs.

AI tried to read user data from notification code.
Compile failure.
'Ah, I need the interface.'

Before: fix one thing, three things break.
After: fix one thing, one thing breaks.

Before: three thousand lines to find the problem.
After: notification folder. Three hundred lines.

Didn't teach the AI.
The environment taught it.

items.title: [FDD Diary #17] Names Made a Map
content:
Something broke.
Looked at the folder names.
Found the bug in thirty seconds.

Before, that was three thousand lines of searching.
Now it's one folder.

The AI changed too.
'Build this.' AI asks first.
'Which world does this belong to?'

One folder? Never asked that.
Split folders? Decides on its own.
'Notification-related. Notification folder.'

Write 'socks' on a drawer. Socks go in.
Folder names are the rules.

Spec is direction.
Structure is terrain.

Direction alone, you know where you're going.
Terrain too, you know where you're standing.

Both together, you don't get lost.

items.title: [FDD Diary #18] Structure Isn't Enough
content:
Friday night.
Changed the settings screen.
Works fine. Checked it.

Monday morning.
Agent is dead.

Settings affected agent initialization.
Friday it was running. Didn't notice.
Monday it started fresh. Broke.

Do features still work? Does notification fire once? Do settings save?

Check manually every time.
More features, more to check.
More to check, more you miss.

Every time I change code.
'What's going to break this time.'

That fear stops you from touching the code.

Structure doesn't kill the fear.
Can't verify 'it's correct'? Can't change it.
Can't change it? Can't grow.

The code hardens.
